## 1. Project set up

```{r packages}
# JOVI's R-version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24)
library(here)        # project-root file paths
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, forcats, etc.
library(skimr)       # quick data summaries
library(GGally)      # pairwise plots
library(car)         # vif() and Anova() for collinearity / importance
library(broom)       # tidy model output
library(performance) # model diagnostics
library(leaps)       # best-subset check for stepwise (not used yet)
library(glmnet)      # LASSO model (section 6.1)
library(nanoparquet) # Reading parquet files
```

```{r load-data}
INPUT_PATH <- "../rea_data/curated/rentals.parquet"
rentals <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(INPUT_PATH)
skimr::skim(rentals)
```

## 2. Cleaning

### 2.1 Duplicates

```{r duplicates}
sum(duplicated(rentals))

n_before <- nrow(rentals)
rentals <- rentals |> distinct()

sum(duplicated(rentals))   # should now be 0
n_before - nrow(rentals)   # rows removed
nrow(rentals)
```

### 2.2 Response variable

```{r response-hist}
ggplot(rentals, aes(weekly_rent)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50)
ggplot(rentals, aes(log(weekly_rent))) + geom_histogram(bins = 50)
```

### 2.3 Listing years

Listings from all years are kept. `listed_year` stays in the data as a predictor
(a time control) instead of being filtered to 2025 only.

```{r listing-years}
rentals |>
  count(listed_year) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

### 2.4 Manual grouping of structural features

Near-duplicate feature flags are merged into one "any" flag with `pmax()`.

```{r merge-features}
rentals <- rentals |>
  mutate(
    feat_aircon_any    = pmax(feat_air_conditioning, feat_air_conditioner,
                              feat_split_system_air_conditioning),
    feat_heating_any   = pmax(feat_heating, feat_split_system_heating,
                              feat_ducted_heating, feat_gas_heating),
    feat_broadband_any = pmax(feat_broadband, feat_broadband_internet_access,
                              feat_broadband_internet_available),
    feat_ensuite_any   = pmax(feat_ensuite, feat_ensuites),
    feat_balcony_any   = pmax(feat_balcony, feat_balcony___deck, feat_deck),
    feat_courtyard_any = pmax(feat_courtyard, feat_garden___courtyard),
    feat_laundry_any   = pmax(feat_laundry, feat_internal_laundry),
    feat_bath_any      = pmax(feat_bath, feat_bathtub)
  ) |>
  select(-c(feat_air_conditioning, feat_air_conditioner, feat_split_system_air_conditioning,
            feat_heating, feat_split_system_heating, feat_ducted_heating, feat_gas_heating,
            feat_broadband, feat_broadband_internet_access, feat_broadband_internet_available,
            feat_ensuite, feat_ensuites,
            feat_balcony, feat_balcony___deck, feat_deck,
            feat_courtyard, feat_garden___courtyard,
            feat_laundry, feat_internal_laundry,
            feat_bath, feat_bathtub))

# Check average appearance of the merged features
rentals |> select(ends_with("_any")) |> colMeans() |> round(3)
```

```{r feature-prevalence}
rentals |>
  select(starts_with("feat_")) |>
  colMeans() |>
  round(3) |>
  sort(decreasing = TRUE)
```

### 2.5 Transformations and factors

```{r transformations}
# Log transformations
rentals <- rentals |> mutate(log_park_reserve_dist = log(park_reserve_road_distance_m))
rentals <- rentals |> mutate(log_weekly_rent = log(weekly_rent))

# Factorize categorical columns (2025 is the reference year)
rentals <- rentals |>
  mutate(property_type = factor(property_type),
         listed_month  = factor(listed_month),
         listed_year   = fct_relevel(factor(listed_year), "2025"))

count(rentals, property_type)
count(rentals, listed_year)

```

### 2.6 High-rent listings (kept aside)

Listings with `weekly_rent` more than 2 standard deviations above the mean are
saved in a separate dataframe, `high_rent`, to look at later in the project.
This is a copy only: these rows are **not** removed from `rentals`, so the
models below are still fitted on them. It is taken before the columns are
dropped in 2.7, so it keeps `weekly_rent`, `suburb`, `lon`, `lat` and the
other raw columns.

```{r high-rent}
rent_mean <- mean(rentals$weekly_rent)
rent_sd   <- sd(rentals$weekly_rent)
rent_cut  <- rent_mean + 2 * rent_sd

high_rent <- rentals |> filter(weekly_rent > rent_cut)

c(mean = rent_mean, sd = rent_sd, cutoff = rent_cut)
nrow(high_rent)
round(100 * nrow(high_rent) / nrow(rentals), 2)   # % of all listings
summary(high_rent$weekly_rent)
```

### Group by year post and pre covid
```{r}
rentals <- rentals |>
  mutate(
    yr = as.integer(as.character(listed_year)),
    year_group = case_when(
      yr == 2025 ~ "2025",
      yr >= 2020 ~ "Post-covid",   # 2020-2024
      yr <= 2019 ~ "Pre-covid"
    ),
    year_group = factor(year_group, levels = c("2025", "Post-covid", "Pre-covid"))
  ) |>
  select(-yr)

rentals |>
  count(year_group) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

### 2.7 Drop columns not used as predictors

```{r drop-columns}
# Removed to avoid problems in the model:
#  - weekly_rent: the raw response (would leak the answer into the predictors)
#  - park_reserve_road_distance_m: replaced by log_park_reserve_dist
#  - lon, lat: location is captured by distance and area variables
#  - suburb: 600+ levels; date_listed: the exact date is captured by
#    listed_year and listed_month
# listed_year is kept as a predictor now that all years are included.
rentals <- rentals |>
  select(-c(lon, lat, suburb, date_listed, listed_year,
            weekly_rent, park_reserve_road_distance_m))
```

### 2.8 Group uncommon property types

```{r lump-property-types}
rentals <- rentals |>
  mutate(property_type = fct_lump_min(property_type, min = 10, other_level = "Other"),
         property_type = fct_relevel(property_type, "House"))

rentals |>
  count(property_type, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

### 2.9 Final checks before modelling

```{r final-checks}
stopifnot(!any(c("weekly_rent", "park_reserve_road_distance_m", "listed_year",
                 "date_listed", "lat", "lon", "suburb") %in% names(rentals)))
stopifnot("year_group" %in% names(rentals))   # kept as a predictor

anyNA(rentals)
str(rentals, list.len = 10)
sapply(select(rentals, where(is.factor)), nlevels)
skimr::skim(rentals)
```

## 3. Train / test split

```{r split}
set.seed(123)
idx   <- sample(nrow(rentals), 0.8 * nrow(rentals))
train <- rentals[idx, ]
test  <- rentals[-idx, ]

# Keep only factor levels that exist in train, and make test use the same levels
train <- droplevels(train)
for (v in names(select(train, where(is.factor)))) {
  test[[v]] <- factor(test[[v]], levels = levels(train[[v]]))
}

# Drop any test rows with a level never seen in train (predict() would fail)
n_test_before <- nrow(test)
test <- test |> filter(if_all(where(is.factor), ~ !is.na(.x)))
n_test_before - nrow(test)   # test rows removed (ideally 0)

c(train = nrow(train), test = nrow(test))
```

## 4. Standardize continuous predictors

Continuous predictors are standardized using the **training** means and SDs
(applied to test as well). Binary `feat_*` flags, factors and the response are
left unscaled. In the plots below, continuous coefficients are therefore
"per +1 SD", binary flags are "yes vs. no", and factors are "vs. reference level".

```{r standardize}
num_cols <- train |>
  select(where(is.numeric), -starts_with("feat_"), -log_weekly_rent) |>
  names()

mu  <- colMeans(train[num_cols])
sdv <- sapply(train[num_cols], sd)

train[num_cols] <- scale(train[num_cols], center = mu, scale = sdv)
test[num_cols]  <- scale(test[num_cols],  center = mu, scale = sdv)
```

## 5. Collinearity

```{r vif}
predictors <- setdiff(names(train), "log_weekly_rent")
full <- lm(reformulate(predictors, "log_weekly_rent"), data = train)

performance::check_collinearity(full) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  arrange(desc(VIF)) |>
  print(n = 20)
```

## 6. Fitting the models

```{r stepwise}
null <- lm(log_weekly_rent ~ 1, data = train)

# k = log(n) gives BIC; the default k = 2 gives AIC
step_bic <- step(null, scope = list(lower = null, upper = full),
                 direction = "both", k = log(nrow(train)), trace = 0)
step_aic <- step(null, scope = list(lower = null, upper = full),
                 direction = "both", trace = 0)
```

### 6.1 LASSO

The LASSO is fitted on the same training data and predictors as the full and
stepwise models. `glmnet` needs a numeric matrix, so factors are expanded into
dummy columns with `model.matrix()`. The penalty (lambda) is chosen by 10-fold
cross-validation on the training set only. Two choices are compared:
`lambda.min` (lowest CV error) and `lambda.1se` (the sparsest model within one
standard error of the lowest).

```{r lasso}
lasso_formula <- reformulate(predictors)
x_train <- model.matrix(lasso_formula, data = train)[, -1]   # drop intercept column
x_test  <- model.matrix(lasso_formula, data = test)[, -1]
y_train <- train$log_weekly_rent

stopifnot(identical(colnames(x_train), colnames(x_test)))

set.seed(123)   # fixes the CV folds
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 1, nfolds = 10)

c(lambda_min = cv_lasso$lambda.min, lambda_1se = cv_lasso$lambda.1se)
```

```{r lasso-cv-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
plot(cv_lasso)
```

```{r lasso-coefs}
# Number of non-zero coefficients (including the intercept, to match lm())
lasso_n_coefs <- function(s) sum(as.matrix(coef(cv_lasso, s = s)) != 0)
c(lambda_min = lasso_n_coefs("lambda.min"), lambda_1se = lasso_n_coefs("lambda.1se"))

# Largest retained coefficients at lambda.min
b_min <- as.matrix(coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.min"))
tibble(term = rownames(b_min), estimate = b_min[, 1]) |>
  filter(estimate != 0, term != "(Intercept)") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) |>
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 4)) |>
  print(n = 25)
```

### 6.2 Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics-bic, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plot(step_bic, sub.caption = "Diagnostics: Stepwise BIC model")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

```{r diagnostics-aic, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plot(step_aic, sub.caption = "Diagnostics: Stepwise AIC model")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
```
```{r}
lasso_diagnostics <- function(s, label) {
  fitted_v <- as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = x_train, s = s))
  res      <- y_train - fitted_v
  std_res  <- res / sd(res)

  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))

  # 1. Residuals vs fitted
  plot(fitted_v, res, xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
       main = "Residuals vs Fitted")
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  lines(lowess(fitted_v, res), col = "red")

  # 2. Normal Q-Q
  qqnorm(std_res, main = "Normal Q-Q")
  qqline(std_res, lty = 2)

  # 3. Scale-location
  plot(fitted_v, sqrt(abs(std_res)), xlab = "Fitted values",
       ylab = expression(sqrt("|Standardized residuals|")),
       main = "Scale-Location")
  lines(lowess(fitted_v, sqrt(abs(std_res))), col = "red")

  # 4. Observed vs fitted (replaces residuals vs leverage)
  plot(fitted_v, y_train, xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Observed log rent",
       main = "Observed vs Fitted")
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "red")

  mtext(label, outer = TRUE, font = 2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
}

```

```{r diagnostics-lasso-min, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
lasso_diagnostics("lambda.min", "LASSO (lambda.min)")
```

```{r diagnostics-lasso-1se, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
lasso_diagnostics("lambda.1se", "LASSO (lambda.1se)")
```

### 6.3 Test-set performance

```{r performance}
rmse_fun <- function(pred) sqrt(mean((test$log_weekly_rent - pred)^2))

r2_fun <- function(pred) {
  # out-of-sample R-squared, baseline = mean of the training response
  1 - sum((test$log_weekly_rent - pred)^2) /
      sum((test$log_weekly_rent - mean(train$log_weekly_rent))^2)
}

test_preds <- list(
  "Stepwise BIC"       = predict(step_bic, test),
  "Stepwise AIC"       = predict(step_aic, test),
  "Full"               = predict(full, test),
  "LASSO (lambda.min)" = as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.min")),
  "LASSO (lambda.1se)" = as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.1se"))
)

model_compare <- tibble(
  model     = names(test_preds),
  n_coefs   = c(length(coef(step_bic)), length(coef(step_aic)), length(coef(full)),
                lasso_n_coefs("lambda.min"), lasso_n_coefs("lambda.1se")),
  test_rmse = map_dbl(test_preds, rmse_fun),
  test_r2   = map_dbl(test_preds, r2_fun)
)
model_compare |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
```

## 7. Which features matter most?

Features are grouped into **internal** (the property itself: type, bedrooms,
bathrooms, car spaces, and the `feat_*` flags) and **external** (location and
area: distances, crime, income, population). `listed_month` and `listed_year`
are treated as time controls.

```{r term-groups}
internal_pat <- "^feat_|^log_(bedrooms|bathrooms|carspaces)$|^property_type"

classify_term <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    str_detect(x, internal_pat)           ~ "Internal (property)",
    str_detect(x, "^listed_(month|year)") ~ "Time control",
    TRUE                                  ~ "External (location / area)"
  )
}

group_colours <- c("Internal (property)"        = "#009E73", 
                   "External (location / area)" = "#D7191C", 
                   "Time control"               = "grey60")  

# Check the grouping of the predictors that went into the models
tibble(variable = predictors, group = classify_term(predictors)) |>
  count(group)
```

### 7.1 Coefficient plot (BIC model)

Each dot is the estimated change in weekly rent (%), with a 95% interval. The
intervals are approximate: they come after variable selection, and listings in
the same area share area-level values.

```{r coef-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
coef_df <- broom::tidy(full, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    group    = classify_term(term),
    pct      = (exp(estimate)  - 1) * 100,
    pct_low  = (exp(conf.low)  - 1) * 100,
    pct_high = (exp(conf.high) - 1) * 100
  )

coef_df |>
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) |>
  select(term, group, estimate, pct, pct_low, pct_high) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  print(n = 25)

coef_df |>
  filter(group != "Time control") |>
  slice_max(abs(estimate), n = 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = fct_reorder(term, pct), colour = group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = pct_low, xmax = pct_high)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colours) +
  labs(x = "% change in weekly rent\n(continuous: per +1 SD; binary: yes vs. no)",
       y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Largest effects in the full model") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 7.2 Importance by variable (partial R-squared)

Partial R-squared shows how much of the remaining variation each variable
explains, on one scale for every predictor. Factors such as `property_type`
count as a single variable.

```{r partial-r2-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
aov2 <- car::Anova(full, type = 2) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()

rss <- aov2$`Sum Sq`[aov2$term == "Residuals"]

imp <- aov2 |>
  filter(term != "Residuals") |>
  mutate(partial_r2 = `Sum Sq` / (`Sum Sq` + rss),
         group      = classify_term(term))

imp |>
  arrange(desc(partial_r2)) |>
  select(term, group, partial_r2) |>
  mutate(partial_r2 = round(partial_r2, 4)) |>
  print(n = 25)

imp |>
  slice_max(partial_r2, n = 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = partial_r2, y = fct_reorder(term, partial_r2), fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colours) +
  labs(x = "Partial R-squared", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Which variables explain the most variation in rent (full model)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 8. Interpretation notes

- Coefficients describe **associations** with rent, not causal effects.
- The models use listings from **all years**, with `listed_year` (reference
  2025) and `listed_month` as time controls.
- Listings more than 2 SD above mean weekly rent are kept in the models; a copy
  is stored in `high_rent` (2.6) for separate analysis.
- LASSO coefficients are shrunk towards zero, so they should not be read like
  the unpenalised stepwise coefficients; use the LASSO mainly to compare
  predictive performance and which variables are retained (6.1, 6.3).
- Confidence intervals and p-values after stepwise selection are approximate.
  Rows from the same area share income, crime and population values, so
  standard errors are somewhat too small.
- Because the response is log rent, `(exp(coef) - 1) * 100` is the percentage
  change in rent.
- Rank variables by partial R-squared (7.2) rather than by p-values, and use
  the coefficient plot (7.1) for direction and size.
